evidence_span.text: In the present study we demonstrate the ability of OPG to support endothelial cell survival, as well as the formation of cord-like structures in vitro using a matrigel tubule formation assay.

reviews.rationale: Model-assessed: the in vitro human endothelial assays directly support OPG-dependent survival and angiogenic cord formation, but not the mouse postnatal brain context.

evidence_span.text: Pharmacological blockade of ANG2 improved brain vascular pathologies in all HHT models, albeit to varying degrees.

reviews.rationale: Model-assessed: ANG2 blockade causally improves proangiogenic cerebrovascular defects in mouse HHT models. The brain endothelial setting matches, but the disease context is not postnatal development.

evidence_span.text: Zebrafish mutants for the chemokine receptor cxcr4a or its ligand cxcl12b establish a decreased number of arterial-venous connections, leading to the formation of an unperfused and interconnected blood vessel network.

reviews.rationale: Model-assessed: cxcr4a mutant data causally support CXCR4 control of brain arterial-venous network formation. The zebrafish system makes the context indirect for a mouse program.

evidence_span.text: This evidence indicates that OPG blocks endothelial cell apoptosis through binding TRAIL and preventing its interaction with death-inducing TRAIL-receptors

reviews.rationale: Model-assessed: biochemical and apoptosis experiments directly support OPG-mediated endothelial survival through TRAIL binding. Human microvascular endothelial cells without a brain developmental setting provide indirect context.
